title: KV cache compaction experiments tracker (parameter sweeps + defaults)
content:
Owner: Samir
TL: Omar
Scheduler hook: Sofia
Perf harness: Marcus / Rina
SRE guardrails: Sean / Allison

Purpose
- Track the compaction/eviction parameter sweeps and what they did to: fragmentation ratio, bytes moved, compaction time, throughput, p95/p99 decode latency.
- Keep a written record of “safe defaults” we can ship behind feature flags for runtime-1.22 rollout (Hosted first, then Dedicated).
- This is not the final design doc. It’s the messy notebook we’re using while iterating.

Definitions (working)
- Fragmentation ratio (FR): 1 - (largest_free_contiguous / total_free). Higher = worse. 0.0 means free space is fully contiguous.
- Trigger threshold: FR value above which compaction is allowed to run (subject to budget).
- Budget: hard cap on compaction work per scheduling window. We’re testing both:
  - bytes_budget_per_step (KV bytes relocated)
  - time_budget_ms_per_step (wall time)
- Step boundary: when scheduler allows compaction to run (prefill boundary, decode boundary, or background thread).
- Eviction: dropping KV pages for eligible sequences to avoid OOM / pathological churn. Tier-aware + LRU-ish. (Pinned sessions never evicted.)

Test environments used (summary)
- Staging cluster: us-east1, A100-80GB + H100-80GB pools
- “Prod-like” perf lab runs via benchmark-lab generator (PR-881) + perf-canary scenario (PR-412)
- Models tested: llama-70b-ish profile, mixtral-ish MoE profile (names omitted here; see benchmark results sheet)

Workloads (we keep reusing these names)
W1: Mixed-length burst chat
- Prompt length: bimodal (short 128–256 and long 2k–6k)
- Churn: high (cancelled requests, reconnects)
- Burst: 3–5x QPS for 2–3 minutes
- Goal: reproduce p99 spikes + fragmentation growth

W2: Long-lived sessions
- 20–40% sessions persist 30+ minutes with periodic decode
- Low churn
- Goal: check for “slow fragmentation creep” + compaction stability

W3: Streaming + cancellations adversarial
- Frequent mid-decode cancellations
- Goal: correctness + ensure we don’t create stalls or allocator leaks during relocation


Experiment log (chronological)

2026-01-10 — Baseline reproduction (no compaction, no eviction)
Run: W1 on A100
- FR steady climbs to 0.55–0.75 under bursty churn, then never fully recovers
- Symptoms: allocator spends time hunting free blocks; we see short stalls around page alloc
- Tail: p99 decode latency spikes correlate with FR > ~0.60 (not perfect, but consistent)
Notes:
- Confirms this isn’t just “GPU busy” — there are visible allocator overhead spikes
- Action: implement FR metric export (ENG-4822 / PR-19342)

2026-01-14 — Compaction boundary sweep (where to run it)
Variants:
A) background-only worker
B) scheduler boundary only (end of prefill, end of decode step)
C) hybrid (background + scheduler guard)
Findings:
- A (background-only): best FR reduction but worst tail in bursts (p99 spikes) when worker competes w/ decode. Needs strict budgeting + priority.
- B (scheduler boundary): predictable tail, slightly worse FR reduction but “good enough” if budgets aren’t tiny.
- C (hybrid): promising but harder to reason about; easiest way to shoot ourselves during canary.
Decision (tentative): runtime-1.22 use B as primary. A can be gated behind extra flag for later.

2026-01-16 — Budget sweep #1 (bytes_budget_per_step)
Workload: W1
Hardware: A100
Trigger: FR > 0.55
Budgets tested: 0MB, 32MB, 64MB, 128MB, 256MB per step
Observations (approx)
- 0MB: baseline (FR peaks ~0.75, p99 spikes)
- 32MB: FR still peaks ~0.70, p99 slightly improved but spikes remain
- 64MB: FR peaks ~0.60–0.65, noticeable p99 improvement; throughput unchanged within noise
- 128MB: FR peaks ~0.50–0.58, p99 best; BUT saw occasional short decode elongation during burst (likely step taking too long)
- 256MB: FR very good, but increased risk: some steps exceeded our “do no harm” budget and p95 started to wobble
Notes:
- Bytes budget alone is not a stable guard on H100 (copy perf varies with contention)
Action: add time-budget enforcement option + traces around compaction (PR-19405)

2026-01-19 — Budget sweep #2 (time_budget_ms_per_step)
Workload: W1
Hardware: A100
Trigger: FR > 0.55
Time budgets: 0ms, 0.15ms, 0.25ms, 0.5ms, 1.0ms per scheduler window
Observations:
- <=0.15ms: too conservative; FR stays high, p99 spikes reduced but not eliminated
- 0.25ms: good balance; FR moderates, p99 materially better, p95 unchanged
- 0.5ms: FR good, p99 very good, slight p95 cost in worst burst minute (not huge)
- 1.0ms: FR excellent, but p95/p99 both see occasional “compaction-caused” plateaus (copy dominates step)
Notes:
- Time budget is easier to reason about for canary guardrails (“we will not spend more than X ms”)
Decision: prefer time budget as primary guardrail; bytes budget can remain secondary cap (safety).

2026-01-22 — Trigger threshold sweep (when to start compaction)
Workload: W1 + W2
Budget: 0.25ms per step
Thresholds: FR > 0.45, 0.55, 0.65
Results:
- 0.45: compaction runs often, keeps FR low; cost: more background work; risk of “always on” for certain churn patterns
- 0.55: “just in time” behavior; FR stays under ~0.60 most of the time; good p99
- 0.65: too late; we still see p99 spikes before compaction catches up
Notes:
- Hosted traffic seems to hit FR 0.55 quickly under bursts; 0.65 is basically “let it get bad first.”
Decision: default trigger FR 0.55 for Hosted. Consider 0.60 for Dedicated (since more predictable load, but still bursty in some pools).

2026-01-26 — Cooldown / hysteresis experiment (avoid thrash)
Idea: Once FR drops below low watermark, stop compaction for N seconds.
Settings tried:
- Low watermark: 0.45
- Cooldowns: 0s, 10s, 30s
Findings:
- No cooldown: mild thrash (lots of small compaction steps) but tail fine
- 10s: reduced total bytes moved ~10–15% in W2 without harming FR
- 30s: sometimes allowed FR to climb back quickly in W1 burst tail; not ideal
Decision: add 10s cooldown (configurable). Keep off by default until we finish canary.

2026-01-29 — Eviction on/off + threshold sweep
Why: compaction alone can’t save us when we’re near capacity and fragmentation blocks large allocs; eviction is the pressure relief.
Workload: W1 with artificially tight KV arena to simulate high utilization
Eviction modes:
- Off
- On, threshold: “free_kv_bytes < X” (X as % of arena)
Thresholds tried: 1%, 2%, 5% remaining free
Findings:
- Off: periodic OOM / forced shedding in worst churn variant
- 1%: still risky; too late to prevent allocator failure in some runs
- 2%: generally prevented OOM; limited eviction events
- 5%: safe but too aggressive; evicted sessions that would’ve survived; can cause quality-of-service issues for lower tier
Decision: 2% free threshold (as a starting point) + tier-aware eviction. Keep strict pinning rules.
Open: Should threshold be model-size dependent? (probably yes)

2026-02-02 — Tier-aware eviction policy (what gets evicted)
Workload: W1 (high churn) + W2 (long lived)
Policy candidate: tier-aware LRU by “last decode time”, exclude pinned sessions, prefer evicting preemptible prefix-cache entries first.
Observations:
- With eviction enabled, p99 stabilized during near-capacity bursts.
- User-visible effect: in synthetic tests, low-tier sessions occasionally lost cache and had to re-prefill (latency bump on next turn). This is acceptable if bounded + not happening to premium tiers.
Decision: ship tier-aware eviction with these rules (current):
- Never evict pinned sessions.
- Premium tiers: only evict if we’re about to OOM (hard emergency mode).
- Standard tiers: eligible at 2% free threshold.
- Prefer prefix-cache / preemptible entries (if present) before active session KV.

2026-02-05 — Scheduler boundary choice revisited (decode vs prefill)
Workload: W1
Budget: 0.25ms
Result:
- Running compaction at decode boundary only: best for avoiding user-visible streaming jitter, but FR reduction slower.
- Running at prefill boundary only: FR reduction ok, but bursty “chat turn” pattern can starve compaction.
- Mixed boundaries: better FR control; minimal impact if time budget is strict.
Decision: allow both boundaries, but prioritize decode boundary with lower budget, and allow a slightly higher budget at prefill boundary (since prefill already heavy). (Implementation detail still in flux.)

2026-02-09 — H100 rerun + copy kernel sensitivity
Workload: W1
Hardware: H100
Budget: 0.25ms
Observation:
- H100 copy is faster but contention patterns differ; compaction steps sometimes finish early, so we move fewer bytes than A100 but with similar FR improvement.
- Suggests time budget is portable.
Note: we should keep bytes cap to prevent pathological “move too much because it’s fast” causing downstream effects (cache invalidation bursts).

2026-02-12 — Tracing overhead check (compaction spans)
Added spans in PR-19405; some perf regression discussion in Slack (1767741120)
Finding:
- Always-on detailed spans cost is nontrivial in CI perf tests; needs sampling.
Decision: keep spans but sample; ensure oncall can enable verbose tracing temporarily.

2026-02-14 — Canary-style guardrails simulation (auto rollback signals)
Goal: what metrics best predict compaction-caused harm vs “compaction helping.”
Signals tested:
- compaction_time_ms_step p95
- bytes_moved_per_sec
- eviction_rate_per_min
- p99 decode latency delta vs baseline
Findings:
- p99 alone too noisy (traffic mix)
- Better: “p99 up AND compaction_time_ms_step p95 above threshold” to attribute to compaction
- Also: sustained eviction_rate increase may indicate we’re too aggressive / too close to capacity
Proposal (for SRE):
- Alert/rollback if p99 decode > +15% baseline for 10m AND compaction_time_ms_step_p95 > 0.6ms
- Alert if eviction_rate spikes above expected for tier (needs tier breakdown)


Summary table (current best-known settings)
NOTE: these are *proposed* safe defaults for runtime-1.22 canary. Final call after perf-canary + SRE signoff.

Hosted (default-on in limited canary cohort)
- compaction_enabled: true (flag)
- trigger_FR: 0.55
- time_budget_ms_per_step:
  - decode boundary: 0.20ms
  - prefill boundary: 0.35ms
- bytes_budget_per_step: 128MB (secondary cap)
- cooldown: 0s initially (consider 10s after canary)
- eviction_enabled: true (flag)
- eviction_free_threshold: 2% arena free
- eviction_policy: tier-aware LRU; premium = emergency-only

Dedicated (default-off initially; opt-in per pool)
- trigger_FR: 0.60 (tentative)
- time_budget_ms_per_step:
  - decode boundary: 0.15ms
  - prefill boundary: 0.30ms
- bytes_budget_per_step: 128MB
- eviction: enabled only for specific high-churn pools; otherwise off until we have customer messaging


Notes / gotchas collected while running
- The “right” FR threshold depends on allocator page size + model KV shape. If we change layout later, we must rerun.
- Biggest p99 improvements happen when we prevent FR crossing ~0.60 in W1. Once FR is >0.70, compaction can’t catch up without large budgets.
- Beware cancellation edge cases during relocation (fixed in later PR; keep stress tests on).
- Eviction is safer than OOM, but it moves the pain to user-visible extra prefill. Must be tier-correct and observable.

Open questions
- Should trigger_FR be dynamic based on utilization (e.g., lower threshold when utilization is high)?
- How do we treat prefix-cache vs session KV when prefix-cache is “shared-ish” across requests?
- Do we need per-model tuning defaults (at least for the very large KV footprints)?
- Can we estimate “copy cost” better than wall-time to avoid hiding in GPU queueing?

Next steps (as of last edit)
- Rerun W1/W2 on latest runtime branch with PR-19371 (scheduler integration) + PR-19388 (eviction) + kill-switch plumbing (PR-19422).
- Update perf-canary thresholds (PR-412) to include compaction_time + eviction_rate gating.
- Decide canary defaults with SRE (Sean/Allison) and product (Nikhil/Lauren) for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Changelog (manual)
- 2026-02-20: Updated proposed defaults to split budgets by decode vs prefill boundary; added guardrail proposal.
- 2026-02-14: Added canary guardrail simulation notes.
- 2026-01-29: Added eviction sweeps + preliminary threshold.
- 2026-01-19: Switched preference to time-budget guardrail.
